guide.summary: Dropbox documents per-user OAuth 2.0 for the User API, and the list_folder endpoints document the files.metadata.read scope with bearer user tokens. The confirmed listing request is covered by files.metadata.read and list_folder/continue pagination. The App Folder file-access setting limits data to the app folder and must be selected when the app is created. App-level client credentials are documented but excluded by the confirmed prohibitions. Provider review, marketplace listing and customer-admin distribution policy are not in the supplied snapshots and remain unknown.

findings.title: Per-user OAuth authorization code flow issues a user-bound bearer token
findings.detail: Dropbox uses OAuth 2.0 so the app accesses each user's data after that user signs in. The code flow redirects the user to authorize the app, exchanges the code for an access token, and sends the token as a Bearer header. The user-token option for list_folder is documented, so this is an individual-account flow, not team administration.
findings.appliesWhen: Each customer connects their own individual Dropbox account.

findings.title: files.metadata.read grants list_folder and list_folder/continue metadata access
findings.detail: The list_folder endpoint requires files.metadata.read and the list_folder/continue endpoint requires the same scope. The scope covers listing folder metadata entries, and the confirmed read-only, no-content-download request uses only this scope.

findings.title: App Folder access type limits actions to the app's folder
findings.detail: During app creation the developer chooses the file-access scope. App Folder lets the app take actions allowed by its scopes only on data within its app folder (/apps). This setting bounds the listing to the App Folder, while the metadata scope limits the action type.
findings.appliesWhen: The app is created with the App Folder file-access option, as the confirmed request requires.

findings.title: Register the app once and configure exact redirect URIs for code flow
findings.detail: The developer registers the app in the Developer Console to obtain the app key and secret and configures redirect URIs. Customers connect through the OAuth flow and do not register their own Dropbox application. Public clients should use PKCE with S256.
findings.appliesWhen: Other customer organizations will connect to the single registered app.

steps.title: List App Folder entries (first page)
steps.detail: Call list_folder with the empty path to list the App Folder root, metadata only. Keep include_deleted false. The response contains entries with .tag, name and path_display, plus cursor and has_more. Map the requested names to entries[].name where .tag is file or folder. A safe boundary check is a request for a path outside the app folder, which should return an error rather than data.
steps.doneWhen: The response is 200 with entries, cursor and has_more. Names are read from entries[].name. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

steps.title: Continue listing with list_folder/continue until has_more is false
steps.detail: While has_more is true, call list_folder/continue with the latest cursor from the prior response. Repeat until has_more is false, which is the documented end condition. Do not reuse an earlier cursor and do not stop after one or two pages.
steps.doneWhen: A response returns has_more false and all names from every page have been collected.
